answer: A robust agent economy defends against sybil attacks with per-identity collateral bonds. Before an agent may earn from the atlas of network activity, it locks a stake on each identity it registers. Honest peers act like a lantern: repeated attestations illuminate genuine participation, while fraud detection sweeps the knoll of duplicate accounts and confiscates their bonds. An attacker spawning a thousand sybils must post a thousand stakes and forfeits every one when caught, so bulk identity forgery becomes far more expensive than it pays.
